clue.text: Removed decoration from grasping male that's not indulged

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it tightly, so one piece closes around another

parts.note: a wall stripped of its wallpaper has had its decoration removed
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A decorator strips a room while a man nearby is left uncoddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed decoration' is a past participle describing walls stripped of their wallpaper; 'grasping' is a container signal, not greed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper is to indulge or spoil, so someone never pampered has not been indulged at all.

clue.text: Second-hand publication from America?

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States
ED is the abbreviation for edition, a published version

explanation.surface: Is a pre-owned book an American import?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'publication from America' is read as an American edition, a US ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods described as second-hand have had previous owners, which is exactly what used means for cars or clothes.

clue.text: Traveller climbing headland shown in electronic device

indicators.note: something shown inside another is placed within it

parts.note: a pager is a small electronic device that receives messages

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upward, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland or cape, as in Sheerness

explanation.surface: A hiker scaling a cape appears on a gadget's screen.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland in British place names such as Sheerness and Inverness; the pager is the old beeper carried by doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone travelling in a vehicle, so the word is a straightforward synonym of traveller.

clue.text: Low moment stumbling upon second-rate fish pie place

indicators.note: stumbling is moving clumsily and out of order, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
B is the grade below A, so second-rate
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A bad moment comes when someone trips over a poor fish pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish pie' looks like a single dish, but the fish is a separate piece and 'pie place' is the definition. MELTON MOWBRAY is a Leicestershire town famous for its pork pies.
explanation.definitionFit: The English market town gives its name to the classic raised pork pie, making it the best-known pie town in Britain.

clue.text: Clay article caught in net

indicators.note: something caught inside another is trapped within it

parts.note: to net money is to earn it
the definite article

explanation.surface: A piece of pottery gets tangled in a fishing net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' is a verb here, as in netting a profit, not the mesh the surface suggests; 'Clay' is used adjectivally.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen pots are made of baked clay, so as adjectives the two words describe the same material.

clue.text: Upcoming stand with the French food

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to bide, as in abide, is to tolerate or stand something
les is French for 'the' in the plural

explanation.surface: A forthcoming market stall will serve French cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a stall but is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibles is a plural noun for things fit to eat, so it serves as a general word for food.

clue.text: Superior to surgeon could be here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: physically above, on top of
second meaning, read as two words: a surgeon may be at an operation

explanation.surface: Someone senior to a surgeon might be found in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AT OP, the answer is where a surgeon would be; OP is the short form of operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior in its literal sense means higher up, so a thing superior to another sits on top of it.

clue.text: Trunk roughly underneath top of tree

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening letter, especially in a down clue

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
or so means approximately

explanation.surface: A tree's trunk lies more or less below its crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' and 'tree' paint a single picture, but the trunk here is the body; 'underneath' places the second piece below the first in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The human trunk is the body without head or limbs, which anatomists call the torso.

clue.text: Official European court located in flawless administrative region

indicators.note: something located in a place is set inside it

parts.note: pure means without flaw
a ref, or referee, is a match official
E is the abbreviation for European
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A Eurocrat from an EU court is based in a model district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Official' tempts as PREFECT, the start of the answer, but it is only a referee; the three short pieces sit inside the word for flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefecture is a district governed by a prefect, as in France or Japan, so it is an administrative region.

clue.text: This might hold oil like fish contains

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an eel is a fish
as means like

explanation.surface: Something holds oil, rather as a fish holds oil in its flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' suggests cooking or oily fish, but it is an oil painting, which an easel supports.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand an artist props a canvas on, so it may hold an oil painting.

clue.text: Pay back rum, beer is free

indicators.note: set free, the letters are loosed from their order and can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Settle up for the round: the rum and beer cost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like the price of the drinks, but it signals rearranging the nine letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse someone is to repay money they have spent, a direct synonym of paying back.

clue.text: Trying pickle for starters?

parts.note: surface reading: sampling a relish served before the main course
setter's reading: a testing predicament faced by beginners, an ordeal on one's first outing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' is the adjective meaning testing, not the verb of tasting; 'pickle' is a fix and 'starters' are newcomers, not first courses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a difficult first experience, originally a soldier's first time under enemy guns, so a hard predicament for novices.

clue.text: Manage reversing AI threat in eventful period

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: belonging to a momentous era

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: to cope is to manage
HAL 9000 is the murderous computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: Handling the menace of rogue artificial intelligence during momentous times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AI threat' reads as modern news but points to the fictional computer HAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal describes what marks or belongs to an epoch, a significant era, so it fits something set in a momentous age.

clue.text: Likely not ably, English investigate

indicators.note: 'not' says the following letters are excluded from the word before

parts.note: probably means likely
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Probably badly done, the English are to look into it.
explanation.walkthrough: PROBABLY loses its last four letters, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to examine or inquire closely into something, a common verb synonym of investigate.

clue.text: One announces coal alternative in introductory overview

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a primer is a basic introductory textbook

indicators.note: an alternative is another version, so the letters take a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spokesman introduces a substitute for coal in an opening briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introductory overview' is a primer, a beginner's textbook; the rearranged fuel goes after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A proclaimer is a person who declares things publicly, so one who announces is a reasonable description.

clue.text: Strange urge in me to abandon university course

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters come out in an unusual order
to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone feels an odd impulse to drop out of their degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University course' looks like one phrase, but the university is the U removed and 'course' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of treatment, diet or exercise, so the two words share that sense.

clue.text: Cut plastic scrap

parts.note: a snip is a cut with scissors
PET is a plastic used for drinks bottles

explanation.surface: An instruction to slice up and throw away some plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb meaning discard but is the noun for a small piece; PET is polyethylene terephthalate.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or fragment of something, which is what a scrap means as a noun.

clue.text: Rubbers from EU country, erasers taking ages to rub out

parts.note: Polish means from Poland, an EU member

indicators.note: to rub out is to erase, so these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
eras are long ages

explanation.surface: Erasers imported from a European country take ages to rub anything out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbers' and 'erasers' look like synonyms in the surface, but rubbers here are people or tools that buff surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Polishers rub a surface until it shines, so in a literal sense they are things that rub.

clue.text: Transport route blocked by a plant

indicators.note: a road blocked by something has it sitting in the middle

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
a way is a route
taken as written

explanation.surface: A road through the countryside is obstructed by vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport route' reads as one phrase but splits into two words with A inserted between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Caraway is an aromatic plant of the parsley family, grown for its seeds used in baking.

clue.text: Told heaviness of sheep as warning

definitions.note: an exclamation used as a warning, not a noun

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the answer is how the words are said

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep and weight is heaviness

explanation.surface: A farmer cautions others about how heavy the flock has grown.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation; 'You wait!' is said as a threat or warning of what is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a spoken threat or caution that consequences are coming, used exactly in the sense of a warning.

clue.text: One mishandling fine glass with tons rejected

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: what is rejected is thrown out, so a letter goes

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A clumsy person drops delicate glassware, with heavy loads turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine glass' suggests crystal, but fine is just the letter F before the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A fumbler handles things clumsily and drops them, so the noun names a person who mishandles.

clue.text: Becomes tearful following bad drink

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
ill means bad
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone gets weepy after a bad drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' seems to sequence the surface story but is the abbreviation F.
explanation.definitionFit: When eyes fill up with tears a person is on the verge of crying, an idiom for growing emotional.

clue.text: Exposed beams and post

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of a covering, so the outside letters are taken off

parts.note: rafters are roof beams

explanation.surface: Bare wooden beams and an upright post in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' seems another piece of timber, but it is the Latin-derived prefix meaning after.
explanation.definitionFit: Post as in postwar or postscript means later than, which is the sense of after.

clue.text: Temperature rising in one's city

indicators.note: in a down clue, a letter rising leaves its old place and climbs to the top

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
a unit is one, so one's can be read as unit's

explanation.surface: The heat is climbing in somebody's home town.
explanation.walkthrough: The T already sits inside the word for one's; it is lifted out and moved to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia on the North African coast, an ancient port near Carthage.

clue.text: Raises as those wanting elevated positions in the Shard take

definitions.text: those wanting elevated positions in the Shard take
definitions.meaning: second meaning, as two words: visitors heading for the top floors ride the ascending elevators

explanation.surface: Raises, as visitors to a London skyscraper ride to its upper floors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shard is London's tallest skyscraper; split in two, the answer is the lifts going up, which visitors to its top take.
explanation.definitionFit: To uplift is to raise or elevate, physically or in spirits, so the verb form matches raises.

clue.text: Name of chap that would be defiant going into resit

indicators.note: the answer goes into the other word to make a third, so taking that word away leaves it

parts.note: resistant means defiant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy's name that would make him rebellious about retaking an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards: the answer placed inside the exam retake makes a word for defiant, so take the retake out of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan, short for Stanley, is a common male first name, so it is the name of a chap.

clue.text: Rich person making rabbit periodicals for Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a bunny is a rabbit; with its opening sound swapped it is said like the word for cash
mags are magazines; with its opening sound swapped it becomes sacks

explanation.surface: A wealthy publisher makes a fortune from rabbit-fancier magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the B and M sounds turns the two words into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneybags is a jokey informal name for a very wealthy person, someone loaded with cash.

clue.text: Still partial to finer things

indicators.note: partial means only a part, so a portion of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone continues to enjoy the good life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial to' reads as fond of, but it marks letters taken from part of the next words; 'Still' is the adjective, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless or lacking the power to move, which matches still as an adjective.

clue.text: Stalk game and be quiet

parts.note: RU is rugby union
sh is the hushing sound

explanation.surface: A hunter tells a companion to creep up on the quarry silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalk' and 'game' paint a hunt, but stalk is the noun for a plant stem and game is rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a marsh plant whose long hollow stems are its stalks, used for matting and chair seats.

clue.text: Advance by women in party working for engineer

parts.note: a step is an advance
the women at a hen party are hens
on means working, as with a machine

explanation.surface: Progress made by women in a political party that works for an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In party' tempts as a container, but the women of a hen party are simply HENS; a hen party is the British bride's night out before her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stephenson was the English railway engineer who built the Rocket locomotive, the father of railways.
